info.name: Inventory Management API

request.description: Success: 200 with {"data":[...]}. Error example: 500 with {"message":"A database error prevented the operation."} if the database is unavailable.
Success: 200 with {"data":{"id":1,"sku":"BEV-001",...}}. Not-found example: 404 with {"message":"Product not found."}.

exec: pm.test('Product details are returned', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(pm.response.json().data).to.have.property('sku'); });

request.description: Success: 200 with {"product_id":1,"quantity":2,"subtotal":"3.00"}. Validation failure: 422 with {"message":"The given data was invalid.","errors":{...}}.

exec: pm.test('SQL function calculates subtotal', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(Number(pm.response.json().subtotal)).to.eql(3); });

item.name: Get product stock status - SQL Function

request.description: Success: 200 with {"product_id":1,"stock_status":"IN STOCK"}. Not-found example: 404 with {"message":"Product not found."}.

exec: pm.test('SQL function returns a stock status', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(['IN STOCK', 'LOW STOCK', 'OUT OF STOCK']).to.include(pm.response.json().stock_status); });

request.description: Success: 201 with sale_id, total_amount, and COMPLETED status. Insufficient stock failure: 422 with {"message":"Insufficient stock"}. Test saves the created sale_id for cancellation.

exec: pm.test('Sale is created', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(201); var body = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(body.data).to.have.property('sale_id'); pm.collectionVariables.set('saleId', body.data.sale_id); });

request.description: Success: 200 with previous_stock and updated stock_quantity. Invalid quantity failure: 422 with validation errors.
Run after Create successful sale. Success: 200 with CANCELLED status and stock restored. Repeating cancellation returns 422 with {"message":"Sale is already cancelled"}.

Expected failure: 422 with {"message":"Insufficient stock"}; the procedure rolls back and the sale, sale_items, stock, and movements remain unchanged. Successful control example is the Create successful sale request (201).

exec: pm.test('Insufficient stock is rejected', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(422); pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.include('Insufficient stock'); });

request.description: Expected failure: 422 with {"message":"The given data was invalid.","errors":{...}}. The SQL procedure also rejects non-positive quantities if called directly.

exec: pm.test('Negative quantity is rejected', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(422); pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.have.property('errors'); });

request.description: Run after Cancel sale. Expected failure: 422 with {"message":"Sale is already cancelled"}; no second stock restoration is made.

exec: pm.test('Duplicate cancellation is rejected', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(422); pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.include('already cancelled'); });

request.description: Success: 200 with product stock and status computed through fn_get_product_stock_status. Database error example: 500 with {"message":"A database error prevented the operation."}.

exec: pm.test('Inventory report includes database stock status', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(pm.response.json().data[0]).to.have.property('stock_status'); });

request.description: Success: 200 with stock movement history (opening stock, sales, replenishments, and cancellations). Database error example: 500 with a consistent JSON message.

exec: pm.test('Stock movement report is returned', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.have.property('data'); });

request.description: Success: 200 with sales, item line counts, customer names, and status. Database error example: 500 with a consistent JSON message.

exec: pm.test('Sales report is returned', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.have.property('data'); });
